title: Heuristic Decisions in Distributed Two-Phase Commit (2PC) Transactions
pattern: Configuring distributed transaction participants to make "heuristic decisions" (unilateral commit or abort decisions) on coordinator timeouts to avoid locking.
why_bad: Heuristic decisions are a euphemism for probably breaking atomicity. If one cohort commits and another aborts unilaterally, the system is left in a permanently inconsistent and corrupt state, defeating the purpose of distributed transactions [41, 354].
detection: Identify methods in 2PC or XA-transaction cohort implementations that perform unilateral commits or aborts on coordinator timeout.
fix: Participants must block and seek definitive commit status from coordinator backups or peer transaction logs, reserving heuristic escapes strictly for manual intervention under disaster conditions.
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, page 353 / passage [354] or page 276 / passage [41].
